boundary_note: Bailén, frozen span 1808-07-22 to 1808-07-22. Replacement boundaries unset; phases are research hypotheses. This draft admits no features, changes no frozen winner and allocates no tactical or campaign credit.

claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 18,000 capitulating troops; side B (Spanish) 30,000.
claims.rationale: Available-for-engagement figures under Bodart’s rounded-up convention (shared research-conventions index), unless the entry specifies a surrender population. Not an opening muster; components are not added twice. English rendering of the claim-relevant portion (ours): "side A (French) 18,000 capitulating troops; side B (Spanish) 30,000."

citations.locator: Bodart (1908), p. 388, Bailén entry; page image inspected
citations.quote: Die Spanier (30.000 M.) unter Gen.-Kpt. Gf. Castaños zwingen 18.000 Franzosen unter Gen. Dupont zur Kapitulation, wonach die französische Armee Waffen und Geschütze (36 Stck.) übergeben mußte und unter spanischer Eskorte an den nächsten Küstenort geschafft werden sollte, um auf spanischen Schiffen nach einem französischen Hafen (Rochefort) gebracht zu werden.

claims.value: Bodart lists side A under Dupont and side B under Castaños.
claims.rationale: Printed attribution does not establish uninterrupted command over this date span or automatic individual credit. English rendering of the claim-relevant portion (ours): "French-side command: Dupont; opponent-side command: Castaños."

claims.rationale: Frozen source convention; success in a capitulation and success in its preceding battle remain separate records. English rendering of the claim-relevant portion (ours): "Victory or successful resistance by side B."

claims.value: Foy reports 8,242 Dupont prisoners on the day after signature and 9,393 under Vedel, disarmed on the following day.
claims.rationale: Capitulation-stage counts, not pre-battle fighting strengths. Kept separate from Toreno’s differing Dupont figure. English rendering (ours): "On the 23rd Dupont’s troops disarmed before Castaños and Lapeña, who had not fought them, becoming 8,242 prisoners; Vedel had 9,393." English rendering of continuation (ours): "On the 24th at Bailén they handed their artillery and stacked muskets to Spanish commissioners who made an inventory."

citations.locator: foy-t4, printed p. 106, Internet Archive leaf 113; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Le 23, les troupes de Dupont, après avoir défilé devant Castaños et Lapeña, généraux qui ne les avaient pas combattues, mirent bas les armes, et se constituèrent prisonnières au nombre de huit mille deux cent quarante-deux hommes. Vedel en avait neuf mille trois cent quatre-vingt-treize.

citations.locator: foy-t4, printed p. 106, Internet Archive leaf 113; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Ils remirent le 24, à Baylen, leur artillerie et leurs fusils réunis en faisceaux sur le front de bandière à des commissaires espagnols qui en dressèrent un inventaire.

claims.value: Toreno reports 8,248 in Dupont’s immediately commanded force and 9,393 in the Vedel/Dufour divisions disarmed later.
claims.rationale: Retains the 8,248/8,242 alternative; no averaging or conversion to battle strength. English rendering (ours): "The first French force numbered 8,248 and surrendered its arms; on the 24th Castaños went to Bailén, where Vedel and Dufour’s divisions, 9,393 men, laid down their muskets."

citations.locator: toreno-t1, printed p. 400, Internet Archive leaf 413; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Componíase la primera fuerza francesa de 8248 hombres, la cual rindió sus armas á 400 toesas del campo. El 24 trasladóse el mismo Castaños á Bailen, en donde las divisiones de Vedel y Doufour que constaban de 9393 hombres abandonaron sus fusiles

claims.value: Toreno names Castaños and Tilly as Spanish signatories and Marescot and Chabert for France; subsequent handovers were separate events.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "The capitulation was signed at Andújar on 22 July by Castaños and Tilly for Spain and Generals Marescot and Chabert for France."

citations.locator: toreno-t1, printed p. 400, Internet Archive leaf 413; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: La capitulación firmóse en Andújar el 22 de julio por Don Francisco Javier Castaños y el conde de Tilly á nombre de los españoles, y lo fue al de los franceses por los generales Marescot y Chabert.

open_questions: Resolve Dupont’s 8,242/8,248 surrender-count alternative against the capitulation returns, separately from Vedel’s force and the battle.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: Foy reports 8,242 Dupont prisoners on the day after signature and 9,393 under Vedel, disarmed on the following day. Toreno reports 8,248 in Dupont’s immediately commanded force and 9,393 in the Vedel/Dufour divisions disarmed later.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Dupont; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno names Castaños and Tilly as Spanish signatories and Marescot and Chabert for France; subsequent handovers were separate events.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Castaños; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno names Castaños and Tilly as Spanish signatories and Marescot and Chabert for France; subsequent handovers were separate events.
